The `POST /api/v1/auth/register` request body.

display name, and public key set all live inside it, signed by the very
key they describe. The server trusts none of those fields until the
signature verifies, so a display name is self-asserted rather than
server-trusted.

post.description:
The submitted profile's signature is verified before any field is trusted;
the `usr…` id is then derived from the profile's key set. Uniqueness is
enforced on both the username and the key: a duplicate key and a duplicate
username are distinct conflicts, so the client can tell "this is already
your identity" apart from "name taken". A suspended key is refused 403
`account_suspended` before either check, even after its account is
deleted.

Throttled per client address (see [`crate::limits`]).

post.description:
Answers 201 with the endorsed `.crisp` bytes; `Location` names the exact
revision just published. A bundle that fails verification is refused with
its compliance report. Throttled per account (see [`crate::limits`]).

The endorsed bundle counts against the publisher's storage quotas: one
that would exceed them is refused 403 `quota_exceeded`, naming the quota
and the numbers, and one that would exceed the server's total cap is
refused 507 `storage_full` (see [`crate::quota`]).

A document an administrator took down is refused 409 `removed` until the
takedown is lifted; so is a revision taken down on its own, while other
revisions of its document may still be published.
